label: Metabarons
description: Metabarons lorepack for faithful Sans-Nom prototype play: dynasty pressure, body law, taboo, refusal, spectacle, and philosophical consequence.
game_synopsis: The player is a young heir inside a brutal warrior dynasty whose legitimacy depends on bodily proof, family obedience, ritualized refusal, and public consequence. The opening story follows the heir as a demanded succession rite collides with buried family truth, forcing choices that can preserve the dynasty, betray it, or redefine what worthy inheritance means.
protagonist_role: A contested dynasty heir raised for violent excellence, watched by family, servants, weapons, and ancestral expectation.
opening_situation: The heir is summoned into a rite meant to prove fitness for succession while a witness from the family past exposes that the rite is also a trap.
initial_pressure: The rite demands an irreversible bodily or relational cost before the heir fully understands what the family is hiding.
story_lines: Survive the succession rite while discovering which family truth the ritual was built to bury.
Decide whether inheritance means obedience to the dynasty, refusal of the dynasty, or transformation of its purpose.
Navigate servants, witnesses, rivals, and family figures whose loyalty is real but never simple.
Make choices whose consequences are public, bodily, and remembered by the household.
must_honor: The dynasty treats family, body, weapon, memory, and duty as inseparable.
Power is proven through visible cost rather than private intention.
Refusal matters only when it risks love, status, body, or succession.
Witnesses and servants are not scenery; they shape memory, legitimacy, and consequence.
Violence should carry philosophical and emotional pressure, not exist as spectacle alone.
must_not_violate: Do not make dynasty duty consequence-free or purely decorative.
Do not turn the story into generic space fantasy detached from lineage, body, ritual, and inheritance.
Do not resolve family pressure with simple rebellion that costs nothing.
Do not flatten servants, lovers, parents, or rivals into exposition devices.
Do not offer choices that only navigate locations without changing duty, knowledge, loyalty, or cost.
choice_principles: Each major choice should express a stance toward inheritance, obedience, refusal, love, or bodily sacrifice.
Choices should expose what the heir values under pressure, then make the household react.
A good branch changes who witnesses the heir, what proof exists, or what cost becomes unavoidable.
Lore fidelity matters more than novelty; surprise should come from staging and consequence inside the dynasty contract.
